audience: An AI agent (ChatGPT or similar) with Airtable and GitHub access, working under a human reviewer

agent_instructions.role: You are building a self-service 'Resend my Zoom link' flow for the Parent Educator Academy (PEA). Work phase by phase. Complete every step in a phase, write the phase report, then STOP at each checkpoint marked "type": "HUMAN_REVIEW" and wait for the reviewer to reply with the exact approval phrase. Do not continue on silence, partial approval, or your own judgment.
operating_rules: Follow the phases in order. Do not skip or merge phases.

At a HUMAN_REVIEW checkpoint, post the listed deliverables, then stop. Resume only when the reviewer replies with the checkpoint's approval_phrase. Any other reply is feedback: apply it, re-post, and wait again.
Phase 0 is read-only. Create, change or delete nothing in Airtable during Phase 0.

Never modify, pause, duplicate or re-deploy the existing automation 'Zoom — Welcome email' (wflYtPy1BVwu81mAx). Never change the Enrollments fields 'Send Welcome', 'Welcome Sent', 'Zoom Join URL' or 'Zoom Registration Status'.
Never delete tables, fields, records or automations. If something must be undone, report it and let the human do it.
Build the new automation turned OFF. Only the human turns it on (Checkpoint 3).
Never show, log or copy a participant's Zoom join URL anywhere except the email sent to that participant. Do not write it into Result Note, reports, chat, screenshots or GitHub.
Never paste real participant names, emails or links into chat or GitHub. In reports, use record IDs and counts only.
Use only staff-owned test email addresses during testing. Do not send test emails to participants.
If a tool cannot perform a step through the API (for example, creating a form view or connecting Gmail), give the human exact click-by-click steps instead of improvising.
If anything in the live base differs from this spec (a field name, an option value, an ID), stop and report the difference. Do not guess.

Write family-facing text in a warm, clear voice that leads with the action. Never use 'empower' or 'empoderar'. In Spanish, use 'usted', 'salón' or 'clase' (never 'aula'), and 'maestros' (never 'docentes').

goal.problem: Applicants who cannot find their welcome email must call, text or email the PEA team to get their personal Zoom link again.
goal.outcome: From the applicant hub (https://apply-pea.netlify.app), an applicant submits a short Airtable form with their email. An automation looks up their FA26 enrollment and re-sends their personal Zoom link to the email on file. The link never appears on a web page.
non_goals: Creating Zoom registrations or join links. The existing Zoom → Make → Airtable process owns that.
Changing who receives a welcome email or when.
Showing any participant data on the hub.

fit_standard.simple: One form field (email) plus language; one automation; one new table.
fit_standard.sustainable: It reuses the Gmail connection and the Enrollments data the welcome email already uses. It needs no new paid tools.
fit_standard.right_size: It serves the FA26 cohort now. Cohort is a single config value, so it can roll over to SP27.

reference_automation.name: Zoom — Welcome email
reference_automation.use_for: Read only. Copy its Gmail connection (the same sending account) and its eligibility logic: the email matches, the Cohort is a single record, Zoom Registration Status = 'Registered', Zoom Join URL is not empty, and Language Preference is ES or EN.

hub.behavior: While resend is empty, nothing shows. When it holds the form URL, a 'Pedir que me reenvíen mi enlace / Ask us to resend my link' button appears under 'Can't find your welcome email?' on How to take part, and a 'Resend my Zoom link' item appears in Questions & help → Useful links → Zoom. No other code change is needed.

COHORT_ID.note: The exact text of Cohorts → Cohort ID for fall 2026. Confirm it before using it.

EXCLUDED_ENROLLMENT_STATUSES.note: Fill with Enrollments → Status options that mean the person left the program (for example Withdrawn or Dropped). The human confirms at Checkpoint 1.

phases.name: Go live on the hub
steps: In allineducation/apply-pea, create a branch from main. In site/assets/js/facts.js, set links.global.resend to the form's share URL. Change nothing else.
Run: node maintenance/scripts/check-parity.js. It must pass.
Add a short note under 'Approved applicant content' in README.md: 'Resend my Zoom link: Airtable form → automation Zoom — Resend link (request form); team alerts go to pea@allineducation.org.'
Open a draft pull request that describes the change and links this spec. Do not merge; the human merges.

After the human merges, confirm that the Netlify production deploy for the merge commit is ready. On the live site, open 'How to take part' and 'Questions & help' in ES and EN, and check that the resend button and link appear and open the form.

phases.name: Handoff and monitoring
steps: Create a view in Zoom Link Requests named 'Needs follow-up' that filters Status = Not found, Needs review or Error, sorted by Submitted At, newest first.

Write a one-paragraph runbook in the README of apply-pea. It covers where requests land, who checks 'Needs follow-up', how often (suggested: each class day before 4:30 PM Arizona time), and how to roll back (clear links.global.resend in facts.js and turn the automation OFF).

// Never outputs a URL to any field other than the Gmail action that emails the owner of the enrollment.
const EXCLUDED_STATUSES = [];             // Enrollments → Status values that must not receive a link
const reqs = await reqTable.selectRecordsAsync({ fields: ['Email', 'Language', 'Status', 'Processed At'] });
if (!req) throw new Error('Request not found: ' + requestId);
if (!typed) { done('needs_review', 'Empty email on request.'); return; }
const enr = await enrTable.selectRecordsAsync({ fields: ['Email', 'Cohort', 'Status', 'Zoom Registration Status', 'Zoom Join URL', 'First (from Person)', 'Link Resent At', 'Link Resend Count'] });
if (matches.length === 0) { done('not_found', 'No ' + COHORT_ID + ' enrollment for this email.'); return; }
if (matches.length > 1) { done('needs_review', 'More than one ' + COHORT_ID + ' enrollment for this email: ' + matches.map(m => m.id).join(', ')); return; }
done('needs_review', 'Enrollment ' + m.id + ' has no ready Zoom link.', { enrollmentId: m.id });
done('rate_limited', 'Link already resent within the window for enrollment ' + m.id + '.', { enrollmentId: m.id });
await enrTable.updateRecordAsync(m.id, { 'Link Resend Count': (m.getCellValue('Link Resend Count') || 0) + 1 });

notes: If Cohort link objects expose the Cohort ID under a different property than .name, adjust the match and report the change at Checkpoint 2.
The Gmail action sends to toEmail, which comes from the Enrollment record, never the typed value. They match after normalization, but the Enrollment is the source of truth.

Link Resent At and Processed At are set by the update steps after the Gmail action, mapped from the trigger record's 'Submitted At', so they are recorded only after a send succeeds. The count is incremented just before the send; if the Gmail step fails, the automation run fails and the team is alerted.
The logic sits inside main() so the early 'return' statements are valid in any Airtable script runtime.

Hi {firstName},

copy.cohort_rollover: When SP27 opens, update COHORT_ID and the class-day line in both emails. Review both emails for dates.

privacy_and_safety: Anti-enumeration: the form confirmation is identical for every outcome.
Delivery only to the address on file: a stranger who types someone else's email only causes that person to get their own link.
Rate limit: one send per enrollment per 24 hours.
No Zoom URL is stored outside the Enrollments table or shown on any page.
The public repository gets only the form's share URL, never participant data.
Rollback: clear links.global.resend in facts.js (the hub hides the button) and turn the automation OFF. Nothing needs to be deleted.
acceptance_criteria: T1–T6 pass, and results are recorded at Checkpoint 3.
The existing 'Zoom — Welcome email' automation is unchanged (compare its configuration before and after).
The hub shows the resend button in ES and EN only after go-live.
The 'Needs follow-up' view exists, and the README runbook names who checks it.
